title: Trial Onboarding Sprint: Outline and Measurement Slate
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a compact sprint-style plan for first-pass onboarding of a candidate open model into Redwood’s serving catalog. Goal: move from intake -> validated trial deployment in a single 2-week sprint with clear success criteria, owner responsibilities, and a small, focused prompt + regression slate. This doc is lightweight intentionally — designed to be used as a checklist during rapid trials and to capture the minimal evidence needed to escalate to a full intake evaluation.

Summary timeline (2 weeks):
- Week 0 (pre-sprint): intake acceptance + infra allocation (tickets created, basic metadata collected).
- Week 1: smoke probes, prompt canon design, latency & cost profiling on small sample workloads.
- Week 2: regression probe sweep, quality thresholds, rollout decision and owner handoff.

Sprint outcomes (deliverables):
- Prompt canon (30–50 probes) covering core verticals + toxicity/abuse probes.
- Latency/cost baseline on target infra (p50/p95 token latency, cost per 1k tokens).
- Regression report (before/after comparisons vs. on-prod model or baseline model).
- Decision memo: admit / hold / reject with rationale and next steps.

Minimum acceptance criteria (trial pass):
- Quality: Automated prompt pass-rate >= 85% on positive intent probes and <= 5% high-severity failure rate (hallucination or instruction-ignoring) for safety-critical probes.
- Latency: p95 per-token response time within 1.8x of baseline model on the same GPU family for matched sequence lengths.
- Cost: projected per-token cost differential no worse than +40% vs baseline, unless quality uplift justifies it (documented tradeoff).
- Regression signals: No single probe family shows >10% relative degradation vs baseline on core task buckets.
- Observability: telemetry hooks (traces, token-level cost tagging, error logs) enabled and validated.

Scope of probes (prompt canon):
- Core functional buckets (example-driven): completion accuracy (20 probes), instruction following (8), summarization (6), Q&A (6).
- Edge cases: long-context prefix behavior (4 probes), repeated instruction loops (4).
- Safety and policy: toxicity classification triggers (6), jailbreak/adversarial prompts (6).
- Low-resource languages / locale checks (4).
Notes: each probe should be short (1–3 turns) and include an expected output signature (not a single golden text, but a checklist of required behaviors).

Regression report outline (deliverable):
- Executive summary (1 paragraph): pass/fail and top 3 risks.
- Probe matrix: table of probes, baseline metric, candidate metric, delta, severity label.
- Latency/cost table: p50/p95 latency and projected 30-day cost at expected QPS.
- Notable failure cases (5–10 examples) with owned reproducer scripts.
- Suggested mitigations or unblockers (prompt engineering, quantization changes, kernel toggles).

Ownership and roles (trial sprint):
- Sprint lead / primary owner: Maya Chen — coordinates decision, writes decision memo.
- Prompt canon lead: Diego Torres — designs probes, collects expected signatures, owns probe repo.
- Infra profiling & SLOs: Liam O'Connor — runs latency/cost experiments, validates trace hooks.
- Safety reviewer: Aisha Raman — runs safety probe sweeps, annotates severity.
- Regression automation & graphs: Priya Kapoor — prepares dashboards and runs sweep script, generates final CSVs.
- Oncall (during trial): eng-sre rotation assigned via JIRA-OPS-17.

Decision rubric and escalation path:
- Green (admit): meets all minimum acceptance criteria. Attach decision memo and owner handoff checklist for longer runway onboarding.
- Amber (hold): small number of failing probes or cost above threshold; require follow-up mini-iterations (1 week) with owner-assigned mitigation and recheck.
- Red (reject): safety-critical failures or unacceptable regression across core buckets. Escalate to Applied ML leadership and pause onboarding.

Handoff checklist (if admit or amber):
- Create model entry in model registry with tags: candidate, trial-sprint, baseline-comparator.
- Add rollout plan stub in Redwood Console: canary group config, fallback variant.
- Assign evaluation owner for 30-day monitoring (metric cadence: daily for first 3 days, weekly thereafter).
- Link probes and reproducer scripts to model entry.

Telemetry and metrics to capture during trial:
- Quality metrics: probe pass-rate, average likelihood calibration for correct answers.
- Latency/cost: p50/p95 latency (in ms), tokens/sec, estimated cost/1M tokens.
- System signals: OOMs, model cache hit rate, batched request distribution.

Lightweight automation (scripts & infra):
- probe-sweeper.py — runs prompt canon against baseline and candidate (script pattern in linked repo).
- perf-profile.sh — bootstraps perf runs at sequence lengths [64, 256, 1024] and records p50/p95.
- reproduce-failures.sh — fetches payloads for failing probes and replays locally.

Open questions / tradeoffs to capture during sprint:
- Should we require an eval owner to provide a prompt-safety-mitigation plan before admit? (pros: early remediation; cons: slows rapid trials)
- Tolerances for cost vs quality tradeoff: how much cost uplift to tolerate for 3–5% absolute quality improvement? Define policy after 3 trials.
- When to run longer-run stress tests (throughput 24–72h)? Only for amber/green candidates that require Dedicated capacity.

Quick checklist (tick-box friendly):
- [ ] Intake metadata collected (architecture, HF model id, license, shard size).
- [ ] Infra ticket created and GPU reservation confirmed.
- [ ] Probe canon drafted and reviewed by prompt lead.
- [ ] Safety probes executed and annotated.
- [ ] Perf profiles completed for target infra.
- [ ] Regression sweep run and report drafted.
- [ ] Decision memo written and shared with stakeholders.
- [ ] If admit: model registry entry + rollout plan created.

Notes to reviewers: This is intentionally terse to be used as a sprint checklist. The goal is to reduce friction for low-risk, exploratory models while still capturing critical safety, cost, and regression signals. Please add comments inline in the probe canon PR linked above or tag the sprint ticket (JIRA-ML-4123) for any disagreements on thresholds.

Small reproducibility appendix (commands):
- Run full sweep: python probe-sweeper.py --model candidate --baseline baseline --out csvs/trial-<date>.csv
- Perf profile: ./perf-profile.sh candidate g4dn-xlarge 256 > perf/candidate-<date>.log

Last notes and versioning:
- This is v0.1 of the sprint outline. After 3 sprints we should collect measured FPR/FNR vs thresholds and update the pass thresholds accordingly.

Change log (recent):
- 2024-08-12: draft created (Maya)
- 2024-08-20: added safety probe tolerance guidance (Aisha)
- 2024-09-03: clarified latency threshold logic and handoff checklist (Liam)
